Macon County is the Decatur area of central Illinois, and Decatur serves as the seat and the biggest city. The Treasurer mails roughly 55,000 bills a year, and the money funds schools, libraries, parks, cities and the county itself.

Find the Treasurer at 141 South Main Street, Room 302, in the Macon County Office Building in Decatur. The phone is 217-424-1426 and the hours are 8:30 to 4:30, Monday through Friday, closed legal holidays. Online payment runs through maconcountyil.us, and the payment site's help desk is 844-400-8880.

Population was estimated at 99,300 on July 1, 2025, down 4.5% from April 2020. The county makes up the Decatur metropolitan area.

sections.h2: Who sets your value, and how to look it up
sections.html:
Down the hall at 141 South Main Street, Room 401, the Supervisor of Assessments answers at 217-424-1364 during the same weekday hours. That office supports the township assessors, runs exemptions, keeps parcel maps and record cards, applies equalization factors and publishes assessments in local papers. The Supervisor also serves as the Board of Review's clerk.

Outside Cook County, Illinois aims for 33 1/3% of market value. You can see your number on the county website, on a mailed notice if the parcel changed or the township is in its general year, in the newspaper publication, on your tax bill, or by phone. Property record cards print for $.35 a page by address or PIN. Sales transfer declarations can be viewed at the office, which helps if your appeal rests on comparable sales.

Your bill equals assessed value minus exemptions, times the rates of each district that serves the parcel. Homes a block apart can fall under different districts, so comparing with a neighbor's bill tells you little.

You get 30 calendar days counted from your assessment's publication, and townships publish on different dates. Ask the Supervisor's office for yours, since the statute allows no appeal once the deadline passes.

Three people appointed by the County Board make up the Board of Review. Between 800 and 1,000 appeals come before it in a tax year, and hearings typically finish by the end of February. Useful evidence includes:

  • A broker's market analysis
  • A certified appraisal
  • A grid of comparable properties
  • Your settlement statement from buying the house
  • Photos

You argue either equity, which compares assessments on similar nearby homes, or market value, which needs recent sales. The Board has no say over the tax bill, so a case built only on high taxes goes nowhere.

The Board sits from June 1 and writes by mail only, so double-check the mailing address on your complaint. You will hear back in one of three ways. The Board may accept your numbers, offer its own tentative value with 10 days to request a hearing in writing, or schedule a hearing that can be moved one time.

Expect a final notice around January. From its postmark you have 30 days to take the matter to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board, which hears it from scratch and welcomes new evidence. Court comes after that, and the county advises talking to an attorney. Property missing from the roll can also be added by the Board, after the owner is notified.

Bills go out in May. The first payment comes due 30 days after mailing. The second is due September 1, moving to the next working day if that is a weekend or Labor Day. Billing trails a year, meaning the payments you make this year cover the prior tax year. You get one bill with two tear-off coupons, never a second mailing.

Late payments cost 1 1/2% per month or fraction, even when only a day late. The Treasurer can give you the exact figure. A bill lost in the mail does not wipe out what you owe. Where a servicer pays from escrow, confirm with it so nothing is paid twice or missed.

Mobile homes run on their own calendar. Bills are mailed in April, the full tax is due within 60 days, and after that $25 a month or fraction accrues, up to $100. Selling or moving a mobile home requires a $10 tax certification.

After second-installment posting is complete, a certified delinquent notice goes to the billing address, with $10 added for mailing and newspaper publication. The Treasurer also prints the owner's name, parcel number and amount due in a county paper. Unpaid tax then goes to the annual sale, where tax buyers bid interest downward starting at 9%, and the certificate goes to whoever bids lowest. What is bought is the tax, never the house.

On an owner-occupied home the redemption period is between 30 and 36 months, and you pay at the County Clerk's office. The payoff covers the tax sold, penalty, publication, sale costs, the buyer's other costs and the bid interest of up to 9%, compounded every six months. The statute generally gives 3 years from the sale but has exceptions (35 ILCS 200/21-350), so the Clerk can tell you which date applies to your certificate.

sections.h2: Exemptions and what changes at a sale
sections.html:
The smaller statutory homestead amounts apply here because no neighboring county has 3,000,000 or more people. A general homestead exemption can take as much as $6,000 off equalized assessed value (35 ILCS 200/15-175). Owners 65 or older living in the home may claim as much as $5,000 more (35 ILCS 200/15-170). The Supervisor of Assessments handles the paperwork.

Seniors can also ask the Treasurer about the Senior Citizens' Real Estate Tax Deferral Program. Affordable housing applications under 35 ILCS 200/10-260 go to the Supervisor, due September 1 of the assessment year.

When you sell, let the title company settle who owes which installment. The new owner should file a change of address form with the Treasurer by March 15, because the address on a recorded deed reaches that office late. If back taxes were sold, ask the Clerk for a redemption figure before accepting any offer. A cash buyer can close on that number.

faqs.q: Where can I pay a Macon County tax bill?
faqs.a: Online at maconcountyil.us or at the Treasurer's counter, 141 South Main Street, Room 302, Decatur. For bill questions call 217-424-1426, and for payment site trouble call 844-400-8880.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline in Macon County?
faqs.a: Thirty calendar days after your township's publication date. No appeal is allowed afterward, so get the date from the Supervisor of Assessments.

faqs.q: Does Macon County send a second bill for the later installment?
faqs.a: No. One bill covers the year and carries two coupons. The second is due September 1, or the following working day when that date is a weekend or Labor Day.

faqs.q: Do I lose my Macon County house at the tax sale?
faqs.a: No. Buyers purchase only the unpaid tax, and you can still redeem by paying at the County Clerk's office.

faqs.q: What is the fee for mobile home tax certification in Macon County?
faqs.a: $10, by cash or check only. Bring the original title, have taxes paid to date, and give the Treasurer both the seller's and the buyer's names and addresses.
